tasks.title: val checked ledger
tasks.prompt: Aether's `parse_int` cannot report failure -- it returns 0 for junk and the numeric prefix for partial input, so its result can never be used as its own validity check. Write an Aether program that uses the CHECKED parse instead to validate a fixed list of Text fields `["42", "7x", "", "-13", "100", "3.5"]`. A field counts as valid only if the ENTIRE string is an integer (so "7x", "" and "3.5" are all rejected; a leading `-` is fine). For each rejected field print `reject: <field>` in list order. Then print `accepted=<n> rejected=<n>` and `sum=<total of the accepted values>`.
tasks.expected_stdout:
reject: 7x
reject: 
reject: 3.5
accepted=3 rejected=3
sum=129
tasks.achievability: verified: reference_solution compiles and produces expected_stdout byte-exact

tasks.title: par shard tally
tasks.prompt: Write an Aether program that sums the multiples of 3 in 0..50 (half-open) using TWO concurrent branches: one covering 0..25 and one covering 25..50. Each branch must accumulate into its OWN record -- sharing one record across branches races and is rejected. Combine the two records after the concurrent block. Print `shardA total=<t> count=<c>`, then `shardB total=<t> count=<c>`, then `combined total=<t> count=<c>`.
tasks.expected_stdout:
shardA total=108 count=9
shardB total=300 count=8
combined total=408 count=17
tasks.achievability: verified: reference_solution compiles and produces expected_stdout byte-exact

tasks.title: array value semantics
tasks.prompt: In Aether arrays are value types at the call boundary: a function that mutates an array parameter in place has NO effect visible to the caller. Print `scaled:` then each value of the first result preceded by a space; then `twice:` and the second result the same way; then `original:` and the starting array, which must be unchanged.

tasks.title: jagged nested grid
tasks.prompt: Aether has real nested arrays; a one-dimensional array indexed twice is a compile-time error, so declare the rank you actually want. Write an Aether program that builds a JAGGED `Int[][]` with 3 rows where row `r` has `r + 2` entries and the entry at column `c` is `(r + 1) * (c + 1)`. Bound every inner loop by that row's own length. Print one line per row as `row <r> len=<n>:` followed by each value preceded by a space, then `total=<sum of all values>`.

row 1 len=3: 2 4 6

tasks.title: bitwise permission flags
tasks.prompt: In Aether the bitwise operators bind LOOSER than the comparisons, so a mask test needs explicit parentheses or it silently yields an Int instead of a Bool. Write an Aether program with constants READ=1, WRITE=2, EXEC=4 and a pure helper that turns a flags Int into a 3-character string using `r`, `w`, `x` where set and `-` where clear. For each of `[0, 1, 3, 5, 7, 6]` print `<flags> -> <string>`. Then print `union=<bitwise OR of all six>` and ` shifted=<union shifted left by 2>` on the same line, formatted exactly as `union=<n> shifted=<n>`.
tasks.expected_stdout:
0 -> ---
1 -> r--
3 -> rw-
5 -> r-x
7 -> rwx
6 -> -wx
union=7 shifted=28
tasks.achievability: verified: reference_solution compiles and produces expected_stdout byte-exact
